title: T1D effector gene prediction methods (Onengut-Gumuscu S and Rich SS)
bodyHtml:
This table displays predicted effector genes for type 1 diabetes (T1D) and the supporting evidence for the predictions. The list was generated by Suna Onengut-Gumuscu and Stephen S. Rich (Unpublished work, 2022). It predicts T1D effector genes at the loci associated with T1D at genome-wide significance in this study:

Fine-mapping, trans-ancestral and genomic analyses identify causal variants, cells, genes and drug targets for type 1 diabetes
Robertson CC, Inshaw JRJ, et al.
Nat Genet. 2021 Jul;53(7):962-971. doi: 10.1038/s41588-021-00880-5.
PMID: 34127860

To prioritize likely causal genes for 65 type 1 diabetes risk regions that reached genome-wide significance, the predictions synthesized three classes of biological evidence:

  1. Combined genetic evidence:
    • genes linked to monogenic disorders in humans with autoimmune relevant phenotypes
    • nonsynonymous coding variants that are either the most significant variant associated with type 1 diabetes or are in high LD with the lead variant in the region, that have established causal relevance with type 1 diabetes risk
  2. Combined perturbation evidence:
    • genes that display autoimmune relevant phenotypes in knock-out mouse models, listed in the International Database Resource For the Laboratory Mouse (MGI)
    • perturbation experiments focused on immune response, identified by literature search
  3. Combined regulatory evidence (QTL):
    • genes where type 1 diabetes credible SNPs effect expression levels and/or differential binding of transcription factors
    • eQTL data were blood cis-eQTLs identified by the eQTLGen Consortium

Evidence scores were assigned as follows:

Criteria Genetic evidence score Perturbation evidence score Regulatory evidence score
Confirmed causal coding variant 1C    
Likely causal variant 2C    
≥ 2 lines of perturbation evidence   2P  
1 line of perturbation evidence   1P  
≥ 2 lines of regulatory evidence     2R
1 line of regulatory evidence with top eQTL     1R

 

Based on the evidence scores, genes were classified as:

Score Prediction
≥ 5 Causal
4 Strong
3 Moderate
2 Possible
1 Weak
